scenes.title: Turn the forecheck into a support angle
scenes.objective: Use a changing forecheck to select a reachable teammate and preserve a reset connection.
scenes.briefing: Navy attacks the right net. YOU control the puck in a wide neutral-zone lane. Gold 1 approaches from nearer the boards, and Gold 2 is near the forward-support area. D2 is closer to Navy’s net and across the middle, while F1 is farther up ice.
cues: D2 is closer to Navy’s net and across the middle.
Gold 1 and Gold 2 affect the support choices.

questions.prompt: Which Navy player gives the deeper reset option?

options.text: F1
D2
YOU

questions.explanation: D2 is the deeper Navy connection in the setup.

questions.prompt: Which two observations help choose a route?

options.text: Gold 1's pressure line
Whether F1 or D2 is reachable
The board side decides the pass by itself

questions.explanation: Pressure and reachability create the decision; the side of the rink alone is insufficient.

questions.prompt: Arrange the regroup scan.

options.text: Read the forecheck route
Compare F1 and D2
Carry or pass, then check the next lane

questions.explanation: The angle is selected after both pressure and support are located.

questions.prompt: Move YOU nearer the middle to compare the angles toward D2 and F1.
questions.explanation: The example moves YOU nearer Gold 1 and farther from D2. Compare the changed pressure and passing angles rather than assuming a safer connection.

questions.prompt: Imagine Gold 2 steps toward F1 while Gold 1 stays at the shown spot. Which current direct passing line stays farther from Gold 1?

options.text: The line from YOU to D2
The line from YOU to F1

questions.explanation: The reset line toward D2 runs away from Gold 1’s shown position, while Gold 1 is closer to the forward line toward F1. Recheck Gold 2, D2’s receiving space and the live pressure before choosing either pass.

questions.prompt: Why should YOU compare passing angles as well as distance from the boards?
questions.explanation: An angle can keep the puck carrier connected to both D2 and F1 while showing the forecheck. If one route closes, the other remains a live branch only when reachable.

scenes.title: Offer high support for a low cycle
scenes.objective: Maintain a separated high outlet while teammates cycle low in the attacking zone.
scenes.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net. F1 carries behind the goal line; F2 supports along the side and YOU arrive high. Gold 1 guards the slot, Gold 2 watches the higher lane, and Gold 3 protects space near the net.
cues: F1 controls below the Gold net.

questions.prompt: Which Navy forward controls the puck behind Gold’s goal line?

options.text: F1
F2
YOU

questions.explanation: F1 controls the puck behind the attacking goal line.

questions.prompt: Which two details support a high outlet?

options.text: Whether F1 can reach a high support option
Gold 1's slot coverage
Following F2 into the same low space

questions.explanation: Carrier visibility and the slot defender shape the value of a separated high outlet.

questions.prompt: Arrange a high-outlet read.

options.text: Locate F1, F2 and the slot defender
Offer a separated high lane
Re-check the carrier and point-side pressure

questions.explanation: The outlet remains useful only when the carrier and pressure can connect to it.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a high support point separate from F2.
questions.explanation: The example stays nearer the blue line than F1 and F2. It moves farther from Gold 2 but nearer Gold 1, so recheck both before asking for a pass.

questions.prompt: Imagine Gold 1 leaves the slot to pressure F1. With the other skaters at their shown spots, which remaining defender is closer to YOU and needs checking before an inside reoffer?

options.text: Gold 2
Gold 3

questions.explanation: Gold 2 is close to YOU on the high side. Gold 1 leaving the slot does not remove that pressure; check Gold 2 and the new line from F1 before moving or asking for the puck.

questions.prompt: How does a high outlet help a low cycle?
questions.explanation: It gives F1 a separated option and can make Gold choose between the slot and the carrier. If the route is covered, remain available or reset instead of crowding F2.

scenes.title: Hold the puck through a line change
scenes.objective: Preserve a usable connection while one teammate changes and the forward options adjust.
scenes.briefing: Navy attacks the Gold net. F3 is changing and unavailable for this rep; YOU carry in the neutral zone, D2 is behind, and F1 and F2 are ahead. The goal is to read possession options as support changes.
cues: D2 is behind while F1 and F2 are ahead.

questions.prompt: Which teammate is unavailable during this rep?

options.text: F1
F3
D2

questions.explanation: The cues state that F3 is changing and unavailable.

questions.prompt: With F3 unavailable, which two pressure comparisons match the current forward passing lines?

options.text: Gold 1 is nearer the line to F1 than the line to F2
Gold 2 is nearer the line to F2 than the line to F1
Gold 3 is nearer the line to F2 than Gold 2 is

questions.explanation: Gold 1 is nearer F1’s direct line, while Gold 2 is nearer F2’s. Compare those pressures with the reset toward D2; the line change does not select a pass by itself.

questions.prompt: Arrange a possession read during the change.

options.text: Locate pressure and the remaining support
Protect or move to the reachable connection
Re-check when F3 returns

questions.explanation: Keep scanning pressure and support while protecting or moving the puck. Recheck throughout the change, including when the replacement arrives; this is one suggested order, not a reason to stop scanning.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a reset toward D2 with a forward route toward F1.
questions.explanation: The example is closer to D2 and farther from F1. Compare pressure and both routes before using either; shorter distance does not guarantee an open pass.

questions.prompt: Before an arriving replacement offers support behind YOU toward Navy’s net, which Gold defender is already on that side of YOU?

options.text: Gold 1
Gold 2
Gold 3

questions.explanation: Gold 3 is behind YOU toward Navy’s net. Check that pressure as well as D2 and the passing line before using a new deeper outlet; the replacement’s exact arrival point and reachability are not shown.

questions.prompt: Why does a line change call for a possession read rather than one fixed action?
questions.explanation: The available outlet set changes while the puck and pressure remain live. Name D2, the forward route and the arriving F3, then choose the connection that stays reachable.

scenes.title: Reset around a crowded slot
scenes.objective: Keep a possession route available when the slot is shaded and a low teammate can become the next outlet.
scenes.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net. YOU control near the puck-side half wall; Gold 1 shades F2 in the slot, F1 is behind the goal line, and D1 holds the high point with Gold 3 nearby. The rep asks YOU to compare a connected reset with the crowded inside option.
cues: YOU control at the half wall.
Gold 1 shades F2 in the slot.
F1 is a low outlet and D1 holds the point.

questions.prompt: Which Navy teammate is positioned behind Gold’s goal line?

options.text: F1
F2
D1

questions.explanation: F1 is behind Gold’s goal line as a possible low outlet. Check the defenders before assuming a pass can reach F1.

questions.prompt: Which two details support a reset?

options.text: Gold 1's slot shading
Whether the low route to F1 is reachable
The half-wall label decides the next pass

questions.explanation: The defender and low outlet determine whether the reset can preserve possession.

questions.prompt: Arrange a connected reset.

options.text: Locate F2, F1 and the high point
Protect the puck from the slot shade
Use the reachable outlet and scan again

questions.explanation: Scan F2, F1 and D1 while protecting the puck, then use a reachable option and scan again. Scanning and protection can overlap; a named outlet is not necessarily open.

questions.prompt: Move YOU nearer the middle to compare the routes toward F1, F2 and D1.
questions.explanation: The example changes the carrier angle and brings YOU closer to all three teammates, but also closer to Gold 1 and Gold 3. Recheck the defenders before using any route.

questions.prompt: Imagine Gold 1 leaves F2 to pressure YOU. With Gold 2 staying shown, which current direct passing line is nearer Gold 2?

options.text: The line to F1 below the goal line
The line to F2 inside

questions.explanation: Gold 2 is close to the direct low line toward F1 and farther from the line to F2. That gives YOU a reason to compare F2 again, while checking the new Gold 1 position and the receiving space before passing.

questions.prompt: Name two support areas in this reset and explain their different value.
questions.explanation: F1 offers a low outlet, while F2 offers an inside option if Gold 1 leaves it reachable. D1 is a high reset to check too, with Gold 3 nearby. Naming an outlet does not guarantee it is open.

scenes.title: Manage the last minute with a lead
scenes.objective: Compare possession options under a stated late-game objective.
scenes.briefing: Navy leads by one with 48 seconds remaining. YOU have controlled possession in a wide neutral-zone lane. The coach asks for a controlled play that preserves defensive support; this does not mean every forward option is forbidden. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing states the lead and remaining time; they are not inferred from the rink.

sources.use: Supports the stated coaching principle. The setup, alternatives and suggested answers are original experimental coaching synthesis, not source-certified.

scenes.limits: Age adaptation and tactical alternatives await coaching review. Static setup: no skating speed, interception timing or uniquely optimal route has been validated. Positional references are examples, not scored targets.

questions.prompt: What score-and-clock situation is explicitly given?

options.text: Navy trails by two with a full period left
The score is tied and no clock is stated
Navy leads by one with 48 seconds left

questions.explanation: The briefing states the lead and remaining time; they are not inferred from the rink.

questions.prompt: Which two cues affect the stated possession objective?

options.text: The controlled support available through D2 or F3
Gold 1’s pressure toward the carrier
A claim that any attacking pass violates the objective

questions.explanation: The lead changes acceptable risk, but the actual available play still matters.

questions.prompt: Arrange a read for this late-game possession.

options.text: Confirm time, score and available support
Compare pressure on each controlled option
Choose and communicate the next support job

questions.explanation: Confirming the clock, score and support and comparing pressure on each option can overlap as YOU keep scanning; only the final step, choosing and communicating the next support job, has to come after those reads are in. This is not a universal final-minute rule.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare the routes toward D2 and F3.
questions.explanation: The example moves closer to D2 and farther from Gold 1, but farther from F3. Compare the changed routes and the clock before choosing.

questions.prompt: With the lead and 48 seconds left, compare the current forward lines to F1 and F2. Which line stays farther from Gold 1?

options.text: The direct pass to F1
The direct pass to F2

questions.explanation: The F1 line passes farther from Gold 1 than the F2 line does. That is one useful pressure check for a controlled forward option; receiving pressure, other Gold players and defensive support still matter.

questions.prompt: How would YOU explain a sensible risk tradeoff without reducing it to “never attack with a lead”?
questions.explanation: Use the clock, pressure, support and likely possession outcome; acknowledge more than one viable controlled play.

questions.prompt: Which call accurately compares Gold 1’s pressure on the two support lines to D2 and F3?

options.text: Gold 1 is farther from the D2 line than the F3 line; check the reset
Gold 1 is farther from the F3 line than the D2 line; check the middle

questions.explanation: Gold 1 is closer to the F3 line. The D2 reset deserves comparison with the forward options, while the lead, receiver pressure and next defensive support remain part of the decision.

questions.prompt: Which two events change the late-game risk?

options.text: Gold pressure closes the support lane
F1 becomes reachable with room
The score stays one goal apart

questions.explanation: Pressure and support change the risk decision while the score remains context.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare forward routes toward F1 and F2.
questions.explanation: The example moves closer to both forwards and closer to Gold 1. Check pressure before treating either route as usable.

questions.prompt: Gold closes F1 but F2 remains open. Explain the late-game branch.
questions.explanation: Name the closed lane, check F2, and choose the lower-risk reachable option while keeping the lead context in mind.
